text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- The cabinet approved a bill making wide-ranging amendments to the Penal Code and determined a three-year development project for the national police. The cabinet authorised Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy to conclude a financial framework agreement between Hungary and the Helsinki-based Northern Investment Bank.
- The presidential board of the Socialist Party will recommend today that a one-day congress be convened for the first weekend of June.
- Leaders of the most militant farmers' groups will meet today to plan blockades of roads leading to the borders and the capital.

- Interior Minister Gabor Kuncze conferred with EU Commissioner for judicial and interior cooperation Anita Gradin in Budapest Thursday. Kuncze requested Phare support for upgrading the technical equipment of border guards, procuring computer technology, document identification systems, and drug-detection instruments.
- Most corporate leaders are optimistic about their prospects this year, according to a poll by the economic research firm GKI.
- State Privatisation and Holding Co. board president Arpad Kovacs announced that the national electricity works MVM will not be privatised this year.
- The National Bank of Hungary has exempted Postabank from its obligation to develop reserves of HUF 30 billion.
- A credit agreement of about DM 285 million extended by Creditanstalt fur Wiederaufbau and Bayerische Landesbank, to be spent on electrifying railway lines in Hungary was signed yesterday.
- The Magyar Kulkereskedelmi Bank will buy a Croatian bank in an effort to increase its presence in the region.
- Three Japanese companies will establish a Hungarian firm in Tatabanya to produce electric cables.
NEPSZABADSAG

- After meeting senior politicians of the European Liberal Democratic and Reform Organisation, Ivan Peto, president of the Free Democrats, said his party could become a member of the liberal faction of the European Parliament before Hungary's integration into the EU.
- PanTel Rt., a telecommunications firm using the nationwide optical cable network of the national railway company MAV will probably be set up in the first half of April.
VILAGGAZDASAG

- The Finance Ministry's management of money owed to Hungary by foreign governments is insufficiently regulated, making the credibility of the ministry's data questionable, the State Audit Office revealed in an audit report examining the period 1993-1995.

- Shares of the bus parts manufacturer North American Bus Industries Kft., owned by the First Hungarian Fund and the bus maker Ikarus, will be listed on the Budapest Stock Exchange this year, this paper quotes a Reuters report.
- Home banking will be available to Creditanstalt Rt. customers from the beginning of next month.
- Porsche Bank Hungary yesterday opened its first branch in Budapest.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- The average yield of six-month treasury bills continued to fall at yesterday's auction.
- Sweden's Electrolux will unveil a freezer factory at Jaszbereny today.
